summary.headline: Overview of Marketing Mail advertising received statistics for fiscal year 2023.

statements.text: For All households, marketing-mail-ads-received was 51,942.0 millions of pieces in FY2023.
For All households, marketing-mail-ads-received decreased by 6,629.0 millions of pieces from FY2022 to FY2023.
For All households, marketing-mail-ads-received fell by 15,739.0 millions of pieces from FY2018 to FY2023.

caveats: Prior to 2007, Standard mail volumes were inflated by about 3 billion pieces due to a double count of Detached Address Labels in the Carrier Cost System, whose volumes are the control for the survey results (FY2008 Table E.2 and FY2016 Table A8-12 notes). The FY2020 A8-12 drops the note but its pre-2007 values are no lower.

Volumes through 2007 were understated by about 2 to 3 billion pieces due to a change in the methodology used by the carrier cost system for estimating deliveries to residential addresses (FY2008 Table E.2 note; also FY2016 Table A8-12). Before 2007 this roughly offsets the Detached Address Label double count; 2007 itself is understated.
Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology (Appendix A8 table notes). Values before 2010 use the earlier weighting.

From the FY2024 report, results are published as pieces per household per year, and the survey contractor changed (NuStats to RCF). The FY2024 report restated 2014-2023 on its own basis, so its values for those years can differ slightly from earlier reports (e.g. bills paid by mail in 2014: 34% in FY2023, 33% in FY2024).

FY2025 used a new survey design (renamed the Household Mail Survey); Q1 was still covered by the old survey. Age bands changed to Under 45 / 45-64 / 65+ (previously 18-34 / 35-54 / 55+), and 'Large MSA' was redefined in January 2025 from the top 30 metros to metros of 1 million or more.

summary.headline: Long-Term Trends and Projections for Marketing Mail Advertising Received from FY2000 to FY2028

statements.text: For All households, Marketing Mail advertising received fell by 8,554.0 millions of pieces, or 14.1 percent, from FY2000 to FY2023, across the FY2007, FY2008, and FY2010 methodology breaks.
For All households, Marketing Mail advertising received decreased by 20,992.0 millions of pieces, or 28.8 percent, since the latest break from FY2010 to FY2023.
For All households, Marketing Mail advertising received declined by 22,423.0 millions of pieces, or 30.2 percent, over 10 years from FY2013 to FY2023.
For All households, Marketing Mail advertising received dropped by 15,739.0 millions of pieces, or 23.3 percent, over 5 years from FY2018 to FY2023.
For All households, Marketing Mail advertising received decreased by 6,629.0 millions of pieces, or 11.3 percent, from the previous year from FY2022 to FY2023.
For All households, the projected Marketing Mail advertising received is 50,617.0 millions of pieces in FY2024, with an 80% prediction interval 43,656.0 to 57,579.0, beating the naive baseline.
For All households, the projected Marketing Mail advertising received is 48,049.0 millions of pieces in FY2025, with an 80% prediction interval 37,768.0 to 58,330.0.
For All households, the projected Marketing Mail advertising received is 40,343.0 millions of pieces in FY2028, with an 80% prediction interval 27,631.0 to 53,054.0.

Volumes through 2007 were understated by about 2 to 3 billion pieces due to a change in the methodology used by the carrier cost system for estimating deliveries to residential addresses.
Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology.
